question: How do autoregressive Transformers learn deeply nested, locally ambiguous context-free languages, and what internal representations, positional mechanisms and robustness behaviors accompany that ability?

key_findings.claim: A medium GPT-2-style model learns to generate long strings from deliberately ambiguous probabilistic context-free grammars.
key_findings.evidence: The main 12-layer, 12-head, 768-dimensional model is trained on fresh samples from depth-seven synthetic CFGs with lengths up to 729. Generated strings are evaluated for grammatical validity, diversity and distributional agreement, and the model achieves high validity on the studied grammars.

key_findings.claim: Relative or rotary positional information is substantially better suited to deep hierarchical generation than learned absolute positions.
key_findings.evidence: Across grammar configurations and long sequences, rotary and relative-position variants learn the CFG more reliably, while absolute-position models degrade. Surprisingly, simplified uniform-attention variants remain competitive in some settings.

key_findings.claim: Hidden states linearly expose nonterminal ancestry and constituent boundaries in a depth-ordered fashion.
key_findings.evidence: Multi-head linear probes recover each token's nonterminal ancestors and boundary indicators, often nearly perfectly at subtree-ending positions. Lower grammar levels become decodable earlier/lower in the network and higher levels later/deeper during training.

key_findings.claim: Attention patterns are consistent with boundary-based dynamic-programming information flow, but do not uniquely prove an implemented parser.
key_findings.evidence: After correcting position bias, attention concentrates on nonterminal ends and neighboring boundary pairs; residual-stream analyses show statistical information transfer compatible with inside/outside-style parsing. The paper also states that identifying the exact implementation is infeasible, so 'mimics dynamic programming' remains an interpretation of probes and attention statistics.

key_findings.claim: Clean grammar training creates brittle prefix behavior, whereas corrupted-data training induces robust but temperature-sensitive error modes.
key_findings.evidence: Models trained only on grammatical strings fall to roughly 30% validity under 15% prefix corruption. Adding 10% or 100% corrupted training data substantially improves robustness. The resulting generator learns a mode switch between grammatical and errorful continuation, and lower sampling temperature can restore validity.

method.core_idea: Use controlled probabilistic CFGs with known parse trees as a laboratory for testing both Transformer capability and internal hierarchical computation.
method.mechanism: Generate effectively unlimited fresh training strings from depth-controlled grammars; train GPT-, BERT- and DeBERTa-style models with alternative positional/attention designs; evaluate grammatical generation and probability matching; probe hidden states for true ancestors/boundaries; analyze attention-residual information flow; and intervene by corrupting prefixes and training data.
assumptions: The designed CFGs isolate hierarchy while remaining difficult enough to rule out shallow local heuristics.
Linear decodability of ground-truth tree variables reflects information used by the model.
Aggregate attention and residual correlations are informative about computation direction.
Fresh synthetic samples remove memorization as the main explanation.
Insights from bounded-depth CFGs transfer meaningfully to natural language and code.

techniques.role: Provides exact latent trees, local ambiguity and controllable recursive depth.
Decodes nonterminal ancestors and boundaries from hidden states.
Identifies structure-linked attention beyond simple distance effects.
Tests whether robustness must be learned from structurally invalid data.
Diagnoses a learned switch between grammatical and corrupted generation regimes.

evaluations.setting: Fresh depth-seven probabilistic CFG strings up to 729 tokens.
evaluations.metric: Generation validity, diversity and agreement with grammar probabilities.
evaluations.result: Autoregressive GPT variants learn the studied hierarchical distributions with high validity and nontrivial diversity.
evaluations.baseline: Untrained/chance generation and alternative architecture/position configurations.

evaluations.setting: Absolute, rotary and relative positions; standard and simplified attention; GPT versus encoder-only models.
evaluations.metric: Grammar loss and valid generation/recognition across depth.
evaluations.result: Rotary/relative positions and autoregressive GPT are more reliable for deep structures; some uniform-attention simplifications are unexpectedly competitive.
evaluations.baseline: Learned absolute positions and BERT/DeBERTa-style encoders.

evaluations.setting: Layerwise probes against known parse trees.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy for nonterminal ancestor identity and boundary indicators.
evaluations.result: Hierarchical variables are highly linearly decodable, especially at boundaries, with deeper grammar levels emerging in deeper layers.
evaluations.baseline: Raw embeddings, earlier layers and simpler probe configurations.

evaluations.setting: 15% corrupted prefixes with 0%, 10% or 100% corrupted training data.
evaluations.metric: Validity of subsequent generations and temperature response.
evaluations.result: Clean-only training is brittle; corrupted-data exposure substantially improves continuation validity and reveals an error-mode switch controllable by temperature.
evaluations.baseline: Clean-trained models evaluated on the same perturbations.

limitations: The grammar family is synthetic, bounded-depth and structurally cleaner than natural language, code or multimodal sequences.
Linear probes establish availability, not causal use, and can learn mappings from distributed nuisance information.
Attention weights and residual correlations are not a unique mechanistic decomposition of parsing.
The model is trained and tested on the same grammar distribution rather than transferred to unseen grammars.
The paper reports that expensive configurations generally were not repeated more than once, limiting uncertainty estimates.
Finite generation samples may miss low-probability invalid modes or probability mismatch.
The current cached PDF is a substantially revised 2025 version of an arXiv record first posted in 2023.
Robustness to synthetic corruptions does not imply semantic robustness or safe recovery from real user errors.
failure_modes: A model exploits bounded-depth or positional regularities and fails on deeper or differently parameterized grammars.
Probe accuracy is mistaken for evidence that the decoded variable is causally used.
Attention maps consistent with dynamic programming are overclaimed as the exact algorithm.
Corruption training teaches a separate errorful mode rather than robust grammatical repair.
Low-temperature decoding conceals a misspecified conditional distribution by suppressing diversity.
Encoder/autoregressive comparisons confound objective, masking and generation direction.
reusable_insights: Synthetic grammars are most useful when they combine exact latent structure with local ambiguity and length extrapolation.
Pair structural probing with causal activation edits or circuit ablations before asserting an internal algorithm.
Correct attention analyses for distance and position biases.
Robustness must be evaluated on invalid prefixes even when all pretraining data are nominally clean.
Sampling temperature can expose latent behavioral modes and should be part of generative evaluation.
Track when each hierarchy level becomes decodable across both network depth and optimization time.
open_questions: Do the identified boundary variables causally mediate grammar generation?
Can models extrapolate to deeper recursion, new production rules and new terminal vocabularies without retraining?
Which conclusions survive on programming languages and natural-language treebanks?
Can robustness be learned without inserting errors, for example through explicit latent parsing or denoising objectives?
What exact circuits implement stack-like memory or dynamic-programming updates?

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Networks and the Chomsky Hierarchy
competitive_landscape.difference: Deletang et al. test 20,910 models on 15 languages and emphasize out-of-distribution limits and structured memory; this paper studies probabilistic CFG generation and internal representations in greater depth but on fewer grammar families.

competitive_landscape.title: Formal Language Recognition by Hard Attention Transformers: Perspectives from Circuit Complexity
competitive_landscape.difference: Hao et al. prove complexity-class limits for idealized hard-attention recognizers; the reviewed work is empirical, autoregressive and finite-length, so successful bounded CFG generation does not contradict those asymptotic restrictions.

competitive_landscape.title: A Structural Probe for Finding Syntax in Word Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Hewitt and Manning recover natural-language parse geometry from pretrained representations; this paper uses exactly known synthetic CFG trees and jointly studies generation dynamics, boundaries and attention information flow.

competitive_landscape.title: Unraveling Syntax: How Language Models Learn Context-Free Grammars
competitive_landscape.difference: Schulz et al. focus on PCFG learning dynamics, subgrammar pretraining and recursion-depth failures; it sharpens the scaling and curriculum questions left open by the reviewed paper's mechanism-oriented study.

novelty_assessment: The paper's strongest novelty is a rich, ground-truthed CFG laboratory connecting generation, layerwise structural probes, attention flow, positional design and corrupted-prefix behavior. It offers unusually concrete hypotheses about hierarchical computation, but its dynamic-programming story remains inferential and its synthetic, mostly single-run evidence cannot by itself explain natural-language Transformers.
reviewer_notes: Read all 46 extracted pages of the cached revised manuscript, including grammar construction, generation tables, probe methods, attention corrections, robustness/mode-switch experiments and compute/repetition notes. Four primary arXiv comparators, including a later direct PCFG study, were checked on 2026-08-23.
